html:
Kalidasa was a poet and playwright who wrote in Sanskrit, often called the greatest writer of classical India. He most likely lived in the 4th to 5th century, in the Gupta age, perhaps at the court of Chandragupta II, but nothing about his life is certain.

His surviving works:

  • Shakuntala, a play about a king who marries a forest girl, forgets her under a curse and finds her again.
  • Two other plays, Malavikagnimitram and Vikramorvashiyam.
  • Meghaduta, "The Cloud Messenger", in which an exiled spirit asks a passing monsoon cloud to carry a message to his wife, describing the land it will fly over.
  • Two long epic poems, Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava.

His style joins rich images of nature, love and longing with polished verse. His name means "servant of Kali", and later legends made him a fool turned genius by that goddess.

Shakuntala was translated into English by William Jones in 1789 and then into German; Goethe praised it, and it shaped how Europe saw Indian literature.
